nodes.title: The four-point inequality from one base point

nodes.summary: The defining four-point inequality of a `δ`-hyperbolic space.
nodes.title: Four-point inequality of a $\delta$-hyperbolic space

nodes.summary: `ℤ` with its usual metric (the simplicial line, a tree) is `0`-hyperbolic, as a subspace of the real line.
nodes.title: The integers are `0`-hyperbolic

nodes.summary: If all distances in a pseudometric space $X$ are at most $d$, and $d \ge 0$, then $X$ is $d$-hyperbolic: every Gromov product lies between $0$ and $d$. Hyperbolicity is a large-scale property, invisible on bounded sets; finite groups are word-hyperbolic for this reason.
nodes.title: Bounded spaces are hyperbolic

nodes.summary: If $X$ is a geodesic space whose geodesic triangles are all $\delta$-thin and $\delta \ge 0$, then $X$ is $\delta$-hyperbolic.
nodes.title: Thin triangles imply hyperbolicity

nodes.summary: The real line $\mathbb{R}$ is $0$-hyperbolic: for all $w, x, y, z$, $(x \cdot z)_w \ge \min((x \cdot y)_w, (y \cdot z)_w)$. On the line, $(x \cdot y)_w$ is the length of the common part of the segments $[w, x]$ and $[w, y]$, and the inequality follows by cases on the relative order of the points. In contrast, $\mathbb{R}^n$ is not hyperbolic for $n \ge 2$.
nodes.title: The real line is `0`-hyperbolic

nodes.summary: If a pseudometric space $X$ satisfies the $\delta$-inequality $(x \cdot y)_o \ge \min((x \cdot z)_o, (y \cdot z)_o) - \delta$ for one base point $o$ and all $x, y, z$, and $\delta \ge 0$, then $X$ is $2\delta$-hyperbolic with respect to every base point, that is, `IsDeltaHyperbolic X (2 * δ)`.
nodes.title: Hyperbolicity with respect to one base point gives hyperbolicity

nodes.summary: Every pseudometric space $X$ with at most one point is $0$-hyperbolic.
nodes.title: A space with at most one point is $0$-hyperbolic

nodes.summary: A pseudometric space `X` is `δ`-hyperbolic (in the sense of Gromov) if `0 ≤ δ` and the Gromov product satisfies the four-point inequality `(x ∣ z)_w ≥ min (x ∣ y)_w (y ∣ z)_w - δ` for all points `w x y z`, where `(x ∣ y)_w = Metric.gromovProduct w x y` (basepoint first, as in Mathlib).
nodes.title: Gromov $\delta$-hyperbolic space

nodes.summary: A pseudometric space $X$ is Gromov-hyperbolic if there is a real number $\delta$ such that $X$ is $\delta$-hyperbolic.
nodes.title: Gromov-hyperbolic spaces

nodes.summary: If a pseudometric space $X$ is $\delta$-hyperbolic and $\delta \le \delta'$, then $X$ is $\delta'$-hyperbolic.
nodes.title: Hyperbolicity is monotone in the constant

nodes.summary: If a pseudometric space $X$ is $\delta$-hyperbolic, then $\delta \ge 0$.
nodes.title: The hyperbolicity constant is nonnegative

nodes.summary: If `f : Y → X` is an isometric embedding and `X` is `δ`-hyperbolic, then `Y` is `δ`-hyperbolic.
nodes.title: Hyperbolicity passes to subspaces

nodes.summary: If $X$ is $\delta$-hyperbolic, then every geodesic triangle in $X$ is $4\delta$-thin.
nodes.title: Geodesic triangles in a hyperbolic space are thin

nodes.summary: Every geodesic triangle in $X$ is $\delta$-thin in Gromov's sense: for every vertex $x$, all geodesic segments $\gamma$ from $x$ to $y$ and $\gamma'$ from $x$ to $z$, and every $t$ with $0 \le t \le (y \cdot z)_x$, one has $d(\gamma t, \gamma' t) \le \delta$.
nodes.title: Thin geodesic triangles
